item.title: Utility Billing Cycle Explained: How Often Bills Come and What the Dates Mean
item.description:
Quick Answer

Most U.S. utility bills arrive monthly, with a service period of 28–34 days — not a calendar month. Some water utilities and rural electric co-ops bill every 2 months (bimonthly) or 4 times a year (quarterly). The dates printed on your bill are the service period your meter was actually read for, not “May” or “June.” Your bill is not misdated — it covers the rolling 28–34 day cycle your utility assigned to your route when you opened your account.
